criteria.saw: The Ti–O octahedra are drawn as shaded polyhedra, which look like rhombi when viewed down c.
The blue unit-cell outline is a square, with a and b in the plane and c labelled at the origin.
Octahedra sit at all four cell corners and at the cell centre, and the centre one is rotated relative to the corner ones.
Every atom and polyhedron sits fully inside the frame, with a white margin on all sides.
Grey translucent TiO6 octahedra are drawn as polyhedra, with O spheres at their vertices.
The blue cell outline is a skewed, hexagon-like oblique projection with a, b and c all labelled in the plane, so it is not a square seen down c.
Octahedra sit at several positions, including the cell corners and a differently oriented one at the centre.
All atoms and polyhedra lie inside the frame with white margin, and none is clipped.
The Ca and SO₄ tetrahedra form a single horizontal double-row band in the middle, with water above and below it and no second band.
Water O atoms sit above and below the band, and each one carries two white H atoms.
The layer runs horizontally across the picture as a narrow band, viewed down c with b vertical.
All atoms and polyhedra, including the outermost O atoms at the left and right, lie inside the image with white margin around them.
A whole unit cell is drawn with Ca and SO₄ spread through its volume, and no single Ca–SO₄ band can be picked out.
Several red O atoms each carry two small white H atoms, which are visible water molecules.
The view is an oblique perspective of the unit-cell box, and no layer runs across the picture as a band.
All atoms and tetrahedra sit inside the frame with white margin around them.
Only black C and red O atoms appear, with no Ca-coloured spheres anywhere.
There are no shaded polyhedra, only ball-and-stick atoms and the blue cell outline.
Each black C atom is bonded to three red O atoms in a trigonal arrangement, though many stray O atoms with dangling bond stubs surround them.
All atoms sit inside the frame with white margin on every side, and none is clipped.
Large green Ca spheres appear throughout the cell.
Green CaO6 octahedra are drawn as translucent polyhedra all over the figure.
Black C atoms are bonded to three red O atoms in trigonal groups, though some are seen edge-on.
All atoms and polyhedra sit inside the frame with a margin, and none are clipped.
Each Al sits inside a shaded maroon octahedron drawn as a polyhedron.
The view looks down c; the outline encloses a 4×4 grid of octahedra at quarter-cell spacing, and the a and b axis labels sit at the edge midpoints, so it spans 2×2 cells with one cell along c.
All atoms and polyhedra sit inside the white margin, with nothing touching the image border.
The Al–F octahedra are drawn as translucent maroon polyhedra.
Only one unit-cell box is drawn, with a, b and c labelled at its corners, so this is a single cell rather than a 2×2×1 block.
Every atom and polyhedron sits inside the frame with white margin around it, and nothing touches the edge.
Six copper-coloured B spheres sit at the cell centre, bonded to one another as an octahedron.
No La atoms are drawn, and every bond runs between B atoms.
The octahedron and the unit-cell outline sit fully inside the frame with white margin on every side.
No B6 octahedron can be picked out; the boron atoms appear as the ends of bonds radiating from La, and the centre is too cluttered to show one.
Many half-purple, half-tan bonds join the large purple La atoms to the brown B atoms.
All atoms sit inside the frame with white margin around them.
The blue cell outline is an equal-sided rhombus with a 120° angle between a and b, and the F columns at the corners appear end-on, each ringed by a hexagon of Ca.
A legend at top left pairs a coloured disc with each label: Ca1, Ca2, P3, F4, O5, O6 and O7.
The hues match (teal Ca, orange P, green F, red O), though depth shading makes many Ca, O and the small F atoms darker than their legend discs.
All atoms and tetrahedra sit well inside the frame with white margin on every side, so nothing is clipped.
The cell is drawn in an oblique 3D perspective as a box with the c edge visible, so it is not a rhombus and the channels are not seen end-on.
The figure has no legend, only the axis labels a, b and c.
There is no legend to compare against the atom colours.
All atoms and polyhedra sit inside the white margin, and none touch the frame edge.
